$comment: Marketplace and platform economies. Scouted 2026-10-25 by a read-only research agent from filings (SEC 10-K/20-F), platform newsrooms and docs. Metrics are not comparable across platforms (payouts vs GMV vs billings vs counts); compare within a metric. takeRateFraction is the base seller rate where the source states one; tiered terms live in takeRate. claimType marks self-reported figures.

rows.name: Apple App Store
rows.takeRate: 30% standard; 15% under App Store Small Business Program (developers with up to $1M prior-year proceeds, or new). Apple says developers paid no commission on more than 90% of the facilitated billings and sales.
sellableTypes: physical goods and services sold via apps
rows.note: Apple newsroom, 4 June 2026, citing an Analysis Group study. Of the total, physical goods and services were $1.1T, digital goods and services $149B, in-app advertising $151B. Ecosystem volume, not Apple payouts. Small Business Program rate from developer.apple.com/app-store/small-business-program/.

rows.name: Apple App Store
rows.metric: developer billings and sales for digital goods and services
rows.takeRate: 30% standard; 15% Small Business Program
rows.note: The digital slice is the commission-relevant part of the $1.4T. Analysis Group study commissioned by Apple.
rows.takeRateBasis: standard rate; 15% under the Small Business Program

rows.name: Google Play
rows.valueText: 15% on first $1M annual earnings, 30% above; 15% on auto-renewing subscriptions
rows.takeRate: 15% on first $1M/yr then 30%; subscriptions 15%. New 2026 structure (EEA/UK/US from 30 Jun 2026; Australia/Japan from 30 Sep 2026): subscriptions 10% + 5% billing fee; other transactions 20% (new installs) or 25% (existing installs) + 5% billing fee; external web links 20% (15% for Level Up / Apps Experience participants).
rows.note: No current official global developer-payout figure found; Google's last cumulative claim (2020, secondary report) was $80B+ earned on Play to date, too old and unverified to include as a payout row.

rows.name: Steam (Valve)
rows.takeRate: 30% up to $10M per game, 25% from $10M to $50M, 20% above $50M; applies to games, DLC, bundles and in-game purchases
rows.note: Valve's 2018 Steamworks announcement page did not render its text and the Steamworks payments FAQ defers to the signed Steam Distribution Agreement, so the tiers are from press coverage of Valve's announcement.

rows.name: Roblox
rows.sellerCount: over 23,500 creators paid fiat via DevEx in 2025
rows.note: Roblox FY2025 Form 10-K. Up $580.3M (63%) on 2024. DevEx rate rose 8.5% on 5 Sep 2025; Creator Rewards replaced Engagement-Based Payouts from 24 Jul 2025. Roblox does not publish a single take-rate figure.

rows.name: Roblox
rows.note: Comparative year in the FY2025 10-K.

rows.name: Roblox
rows.note: Context for DevEx: 2025 revenue was $4,890.6M; average DAUs 127M.

rows.name: Fortnite creator economy (Epic Games)
rows.note: Epic's Fortnite Ecosystem 2024 Year in Review (22 Jan 2025). Page returned 403 to direct fetch; figures read from the page's indexed text and matched by Tubefilter/GamesBeat. No 2025 year-in-review found. Engagement-payout share of net revenue not verified, so takeRate left null.

rows.name: Fortnite creator economy (Epic Games)
rows.metric: cumulative payouts to UEFN creators since 2023
rows.note: Epic State of Unreal 2026 recap; page returned 403 to direct fetch, figure read from its indexed text and matched by GamesBeat and PocketGamer (17 Jun 2026). Threshold reportedly crossed in Jan 2026.

rows.name: Epic Games Store
rows.valueText: 12% (developer keeps 88%); 0% on first $1M net revenue per product per year
rows.takeRate: 0% on first $1M net revenue per product per calendar year (reset each 1 Jan from 2026), then 12%
rows.note: Read from Epic's announcement via search excerpt. Automatic, per title; Epic First Run gives 100% for six months.
rows.takeRateBasis: after the first $1M per product per year

rows.name: Fab (Epic Games asset marketplace)
rows.valueText: sellers receive 88% of product sales revenue
rows.takeRate: 12% (seller 88%); payouts 30 days after month end, $100 minimum
rows.note: Fab merged Unreal Engine Marketplace, ArtStation Marketplace, Sketchfab and Quixel; launched Oct 2024. Read via search excerpt of Fab publisher pages. No published seller-earnings total.

rows.name: Shopify
rows.sellerCount: millions of merchants in more than 175 countries (as of 31 Dec 2025)
rows.note: Shopify FY2025 10-K. $248.1B of GMV was processed via Shopify Payments. Shopify gives no exact merchant count.

rows.name: Shopify
rows.note: Comparative year in the FY2025 10-K.

rows.name: Shopify App Store
rows.takeRate: 0% on first $1M lifetime gross app revenue earned from 1 Jan 2025, 15% above; 15% on all revenue for developers with $20M+ prior-year App Store earnings or $100M+ company revenue; plus 2.9% processing fee
rows.sellerCount: more than 21,000 apps in the Shopify App Store (31 Dec 2025, per 10-K)
rows.note: Shopify newsroom post dated 28 Jul 2026: 'the $1.3 billion the app ecosystem earned last year'. Same post says the partner ecosystem generated $6.86 per $1 of Shopify revenue in 2025. Revenue-share terms from shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/distribution/revenue-share.

rows.name: Etsy, Inc. (Etsy, Depop, Reverb)
rows.takeRate: Etsy marketplace: 6.5% transaction fee on item price plus shipping and gift wrap, $0.20 listing fee, plus payment processing (US example 3% + $0.25); Offsite Ads 15% (12% for some sellers)
rows.note: Etsy FY2025 10-K. Includes Reverb until its sale on 2 Jun 2025. Fee terms from etsy.com/legal/fees (updated 5 Oct 2026), read via search excerpt because the page returned 403.

rows.name: Etsy marketplace
rows.takeRate: 6.5% transaction fee + $0.20 listing fee + payment processing
rows.sellerCount: 5.6 million active sellers; 86.5 million active buyers (31 Dec 2025)
rows.note: Etsy FY2025 10-K.
rows.takeRateBasis: transaction fee only; listing and processing fees extra

rows.name: Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing (KDP)
rows.metric: total KDP Kindle+ author earnings (one month)
rows.takeRate: eBook royalty 70% of list price less delivery costs, or 35% of list price
rows.note: KDP page reads 'Total KDP Kindle+ Author Earnings for September are $69.3 Million'. Year not printed; taken as Sept 2026 from the retrieval date. 'Kindle+' is the page's term; it appears to be the page-read subscription programme formerly reported as Kindle Unlimited, but that link is not stated. No annual total published.
rows.takeRateBasis: eBooks on the 70% royalty plan, before delivery costs

rows.name: Envato
rows.note: envato.com/about now redirects to elements.envato.com/about, which states '$1.4B contributor earnings' with no date range. In 2020 Envato reported passing $1B with 81,000 creators (Startup Daily, secondary). Author fee rates vary by item and exclusivity and were not verified.
rows.claimType: self-reported marketing figure, unaudited or undated

rows.name: Creative Market
rows.valueText: over $165 million over the platform's lifetime
rows.sellerCount: press release announced 5,000 new shops; network of 11 million members (sell page)
rows.note: Company press release via ACCESSWIRE, 25 Jun 2024. Commission rate not stated on creativemarket.com/sell.
rows.claimType: self-reported marketing figure, unaudited or undated

rows.name: Gumroad
rows.valueText: 10% + $0.50 per direct sale; 30% on Discover marketplace sales
rows.takeRate: 10% + $0.50 (profile or direct links); 30% (Discover marketplace)
rows.note: No total creator earnings figure on the pricing page.

rows.name: Whop
rows.valueText: over $2 billion paid out to creators
rows.takeRate: platform fee on most transactions plus processing; rate not stated on cited page (Sacra, secondary, reports a 3% base fee and the Discover marketplace fee cut from 30% to 0% in May 2025)
rows.note: Self-reported marketing claim in a Whop blog post dated 11 Feb 2026; unaudited.
rows.claimType: self-reported marketing figure, unaudited or undated

rows.name: Patreon
rows.metric: cumulative payments from fans to creators
rows.takeRate: 10% platform fee for creators launching after 4 Aug 2025 (earlier creators keep legacy pricing, e.g. 8% Pro, 12% Premium), plus payment processing
rows.note: Milestone announced 5 Aug 2025. Fee from Patreon help article 36426991446797, read via search excerpt (direct fetch 403). The 'over $2B a year' figure seen in secondary sources was not verified.

rows.name: Substack
rows.takeRate: 10% of subscription revenue plus payment processing (per secondary sources; not stated on the cited post)
rows.note: Counts subscriptions, not unique payers. No later official milestone found.

rows.name: YouTube
rows.metric: payouts to creators, artists and media companies
rows.valueText: over $100 billion in the past four years
rows.takeRate: not stated in source (YPP long-form ad share is commonly cited as 55% to creators; not verified here)
rows.note: Neal Mohan letter dated 21 Jan 2026. Includes music labels and media companies, not only independent creators. The 2024 letter cited over $70B over three years.

rows.name: Spotify
rows.metric: royalty payouts to the music industry
rows.sellerCount: more than 1,500 artists generated over $1M in royalties from Spotify in 2025 (Loud & Clear takeaways)
rows.note: Paid to rightsholders (labels, distributors, publishers), not directly to artists. Loud & Clear 2026 (March 2026) repeats the figure; roughly half generated by independent artists and labels.

rows.name: Spotify
rows.metric: cumulative payouts to artists, songwriters and rightsholders
rows.note: Stated as 'nearly $70 billion', so the value is an upper bound, not exact.

rows.name: Bandcamp
rows.metric: cumulative fan payments to artists and labels
rows.takeRate: 15% on digital items (10% after an artist passes $5,000 in sales); 10% on physical items; waived on Bandcamp Fridays
rows.note: About page says an average of 82% of each sale goes to the artist or label. Fees from get.bandcamp.help/hc/articles/23020694353047.

rows.name: Bandcamp
rows.metric: fan spend in the past year
rows.takeRate: 15% digital / 10% physical
rows.note: 'In the past year alone, they've spent $225 million.' Exact window not stated.

rows.name: DistroKid
rows.valueText: EUR 23.99 per year (EUR 2/month), artists keep 100% of earnings
rows.takeRate: 0% of royalties; flat annual fee
sellableTypes: music distribution to streaming and download stores
rows.note: Price shown in EUR for this locale. DistroKid publishes no payout total or artist count.

rows.name: Fiverr
rows.takeRate: 27.7% (marketplace revenue / GMV); 27.6% in 2024
rows.sellerCount: 3.1 million annual active buyers at 31 Dec 2025, $342 annual spend per buyer (company results release)
sellableTypes: freelance services (Gigs): design, writing, programming, video, AI services, marketing
rows.note: Fiverr FY2025 20-F, read via search excerpt. Absolute 2025 GMV not found in a fetched primary page, so no GMV row. Buyer figures from the Q4/FY2025 release (investors.fiverr.com returned 403).

rows.name: Upwork
rows.takeRate: marketplace take rate 18.7% (2025) vs 18.0% (2024)
rows.note: Upwork FY2025 10-K. 2024 GSV was $4,008.1M.

rows.name: Hugging Face Hub
rows.note: Live count from the models listing. Hugging Face has no general paid model marketplace with a published seller revenue share, so this is a distribution and supply metric, not a payout economy.

rows.name: AWS Marketplace
rows.valueText: 3% (SaaS and AWS Data Exchange public offers)
rows.takeRate: SaaS public 3%; server products (AMI, container, ML) 20%; private offers 3% under $1M TCV, 2% $1M to under $10M, 1.5% at $10M+, renewals 1.5%; CPPO +0.5%; professional services 0.5% (0% in qualifying bundles); South Korea +1% from 1 Apr 2025
rows.note: AWS publishes no current seller-payout total in the cited docs.

rows.name: Apify Store
rows.valueText: more than $4 million since Apify Store launched
rows.takeRate: 80% to developer
rows.note: Apify press release (syndicated). Same release: over $563,000 paid to community developers in September 2025 alone.

rows.name: RapidAPI Hub
rows.valueText: 25% on all payments through the API Hub
rows.takeRate: 25% (was 20% before 15 Nov 2025); PayPal payout fees extra
rows.note: Does not apply to Enterprise Hub customers.

rows.name: Notion Marketplace
rows.takeRate: 8% + $0.40; 1% FX fee for non-US payouts; 14-day hold
rows.note: Some localized versions of the help page still say 10% + $0.40; the English page says 8%.

rows.name: Framer Marketplace
rows.takeRate: 0% cut on Marketplace sales; referral commission up to 50% of referred subscriptions for 12 months
rows.note: Same page: '$753,000 total paid out to creators in November' (year not stated). Payouts include referral commissions, not only template sales.

rows.name: Webflow Marketplace
rows.takeRate: 5% (creator 95%); fulfillment links allow selling outside the Marketplace
rows.note: Webflow pages failed direct fetch (header overflow); rate read from the official update page's indexed text. Older sources citing 80% are outdated.

rows.name: Unity Asset Store
rows.valueText: Unity pays providers 70% of the sales price
rows.takeRate: 30% (provider 70%, net of refunds, bank fees and taxes); 100% of Program Funds
rows.note: Section 4.3 of the Asset Store Provider Agreement. No published total of provider earnings.

rows.name: Gumroad
rows.takeRate: 10% + $0.50 (profile or direct links); 30% (Discover marketplace)
rows.note: Same pricing page as gumroad-fee. Whether processing is included is not stated.
